doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Music in the house: Lawrence Welk and country shows
summary: Little music at home beyond Welk and country shows on television; music came from outside.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What kind of music was in your household when you were growing up as a kid?

I remember on the television, I remember distinctly, I remember two things, I remember Lawrence Welk was on the television and then there was a lot of country music on the television. I remember at the time there was these sort of country shows and there was like a young girl, I think a brother and sister that played like guitars and mandolins and they used to play double neck things, like mandolin on one and then six string on the other. And they were like, three feet high, I mean these were kids. And they were playing faster than the speed of light. They were playing all these country rags. But this wasn’t

music that my parents listened to, we didn’t really have music in the house in terms of there was no, there was a victrola I guess, not a wind-up kind I mean you actually plugged it in and it went around, you didn’t have to crank it up, you know, I’m not quite that old. So they bought me a record player. I think the music came from outside the house. Because the only music in the house really was Lawrence and this country stuff. And I knew pretty early on that Lawrence wasn’t for me. I don’t know, something just didn’t click. I didn’t get it. I later learned to like champagne a little bit, you know, from the champagne ladies, and all the bubbles, but I didn’t really—
